title: Guaranteed serve window and proportional credit schedule for Dedicated pools
creator: Priya Nair
description: Define a contractual SLA and error-budget model for Dedicated GPU pools that balances predictable throughput commitments with automated autoscaling and proportional crediting when shortfalls occur.
background: Customers purchasing Dedicated capacity require a simple, auditable commitment they can reference in contracts. Existing internal work covers raw throughput measurement and autoscale controls, but there is no single customer-facing definition that ties measurement windows, acceptable degradation, and crediting to fleet-level autoscaling behavior and fallbacks.
goals: Ship a single-page SLA definition that non-engineering stakeholders (legal, sales, finance) can include in quotes
Define measurable error budget and credit formulas tied to per-customer reserved throughput and fleet-level serve windows
Specify how autoscaling and burst policies affect measurement and remediation (when to trigger credits vs. when to apply mitigation)
Include a short remediation/playbook flow for customers and support teams that covers detection, notification, and credit settlement
non_goals: Designing enforcement mechanisms for admission control (handled by ENG tickets)
Replacing existing enterprise negotiation clauses for highly-customized contracts
success_metrics: Complete a contract-ready SLA doc reviewed by Legal and Sales by 2025-03-15
Reduce ambiguity incidents escalated to Legal from pricing teams by 80% within two quarters
Implement credit calculation spec that maps 1:1 to billing system fields (billing integration ticket created)
acceptance_criteria: One-page customer SLA PDF and plain-language appendix available in Confluence
Credit calculation examples (3 scenarios: transient spike, sustained degradation, planned maintenance) included
Automated measurement definition (metrics, windows, sampling frequency) specified and approved by ENG owners
On-call playbook and notification templates provided for Support and Customer Success
implementation_notes: Measure at the reservation level: committed_rps and observed_95th_percentile_rps over a rolling 1h window
Error budget defined as allowable percent below committed_rps per 1h window (default 7%) with escalation at 20% burn
Credits computed proportionally to the relative shortfall and number of affected windows during the billing period
Autoscale events that add capacity within the same 1h window reduce the shortfall proportionally; bursts served from burst pool count as served for measurement purposes if they meet latency SLO
Fallback to compatible model variants (lower-throughput/quantized) only applies to availability SLA, not throughput crediting unless explicitly accepted in the contract
open_questions: Should planned maintenance be excluded automatically or require a 72h notice to qualify for exclusion?
Do we allow customers to opt into a higher-availability tier (smaller error budget) for additional fee?
How do we treat multi-region deployments where one region degrades but another compensates?
risks: Too-generous credit formula could materially increase short-term payouts when fleet-wide events occur
Tight measurement windows may cause noise and micro-credits; need smoothing rules
Legal may push for longer notice windows or different definitions that conflict with engineering telemetry
tasks: Draft SLA one-pager and plain-language appendix (PM)
Propose measurement spec and example queries for ENG to implement (PM + ENG)
Run 3 retrospective scenarios against last 12 months of telemetry to validate credit exposure (ENG + Finance)
Publish SLA and update sales quoting templates (Sales Ops)
Create Support playbook and notification templates (Support + PM)
